title: Welcome!
text:
Welcome to my (Ryan K. Murphy) research website!
I’m a graduate researcher interested in amphibian ecology, behavior, chemical ecology, and conservation biology.
My research focuses on using interdisciplinary integrative approaches to understand how environmental change and species interactions (both natural and anthropogenic) influence amphibians and their populations.

title: Welcome!
text:
Current Research

Mazama Newt Conservation
I’m currently studying the ecology and conservation of Mazama newts (Taricha granulosa mazamae) in Crater Lake, Oregon.
My research interests include:

Predator-prey interactions
Population ecology and demographics
Conservation genetics
Reproductive biology and life history
Chemical ecology

title: Welcome!
text:
Past Research

Organismal Responses of Pacific Newts (Taricha spp.) to Natural and Anthropogenic Threats
This research involved using chemical cues to determine how newts responded (both behaviorally and physiologically) to different threats, including:

Native snake (Thamnophis spp.)
Native fish (Oncorhynchus spp.)
Invasive fish (Gambusia spp.)
Invasive crayfish (Pacifasticus spp.)
Fire (ash)
Agricultural runoff (Ammonium Nitrate)
Pesticide (Glyphosate)
